notes: MRQ-224 owns the post-deadline participant-model band in EVALUATION §2.12: the public form's participant list and on-behalf-of disclosure, task_templates.applies_to_roles and its copy-manifest entry, the intake trust guard, the one role authority read by the three work fan-outs, the inverted decision-recipient ladder, the untruncated person-conflict loop, and participation.role on the public projection. AC-272 was satisfied by MRQ-160/MRQ-162 before this band and is recorded rather than rebuilt; its fan-out half (an off-stage submitter is assigned no tasks) is asserted here. AC-223 and AC-224 are the post-competition criteria this band promotes into AC-271; they carry no EVALUATION row of their own and so are deliberately absent from the exercise list. Residuals for handoff. (1) RULED 2026-08-16: a membership row is a seat at the event, not a claim to be a speaker. Migration 0028 widens memberships.role to mirror the on-stage half of participations.role and the acceptance cascade writes the role the seat was earned in; speaker-only surfaces filter that role, seat surfaces filter the on-stage set, and staff surfaces exclude it rather than testing <> 'speaker'. speakers-roster.MRQ-111.test.ts asserts both halves in one test. (2) The submitter is deliberately kept in CALENDAR_PARTICIPATION_ROLES and nowhere else in the work fan-out, because AC-328 binds a calendar-recipient submitter by name. (3) NARROWING A TEMPLATE DOES NOT WITHDRAW TASKS ALREADY ASSIGNED: reconcileTaskSet inserts and restores but never cancels, so an organizer who retargets a template leaves the existing holders' open tasks in place. The Settings copy now says so rather than implying otherwise; cancelling on narrow is a destructive cascade that wants the reversal dialog's treatment and its own ticket. (4) Autosave rewrites a draft's answers and participations from the request rather than merging into the stored set, so a partial PATCH drops what it omits. Pre-existing on this route and unchanged here; the shipped client always sends the whole form.
